key_insight: The paper embeds complex multi-material packaging geometry in a background mesh and uses CutFEM with Nitsche interface coupling to simulate transient heat conduction without body-fitted meshing.
engineering_relevance: This enables more practical and scalable thermal analysis of advanced electronic packages with intricate material interfaces, which is critical for design and reliability assessment.
method: Unfitted CutFEM on a regular background mesh for heterogeneous package geometries
Coefficient-weighted symmetric Nitsche enforcement of interface temperature and heat-flux continuity
Ghost-penalty stabilization to handle small cut cells and improve robustness
evidence_signal: The method is validated on 2D and 3D package benchmarks with substrate, molding compound, die, and solder balls, and includes semi-discrete, fully discrete, and energy-estimate analysis.
watch_item: Accuracy and stability still depend on careful stabilization and interface treatment when physical domains intersect the background mesh with very small cuts.
paper_title: A Cut Finite Element Method for Transient Thermal Simulation in Multi-material Electronic Packaging Structures
